comments.body:
## Phase 1 RCA — mechanism proven; classified `incomplete-implementation` (cited); ESCALATED on AC3 design decision

Investigated under /rebar-debug in a fresh worktree off `origin/main`
(`565e1856bc9d180876fdbcaa336ccd57ceb8202e`; the 2337 fix `83edf99` is an ancestor).
Step 0: no duplicate ticket; sole report. Reported-against floor = current `origin/main`.

### Proven mechanism (the guards are genuinely ABSENT — an omission, not broken behaviour)

- **AC1/AC2 (mint-time warning) — absent.** `sign_manifest` → `_sign_manifest_under_lock` →
  `_prepare_manifest_event` → `mint_opcert_record` (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:293`) resolves
  the signing key via `ensure_opcert_key`/`_opcert_own_key_paths` and mints, but never invokes the
  verify-side resolver `_opcert_own_public_keys` to check whether a public counterpart is
  resolvable. Confirmed statically: `_opcert_own_public_keys` has exactly ONE caller —
  `verify_opcert_record` (`_opcert_signing.py:550`) — and none on the mint path. So no warning is
  emitted when the public half is unresolvable.
- **AC3 (startup/deploy health check) — absent.** No public-counterpart / `_opcert_own_*` /
  `_read_opcert_pub` check exists anywhere in `mcp_server.py`, `_mcp_health.py`, or
  `_opcert_binding.py` (grep: zero hits). `compose_startup_opcert_binding` (`mcp_server.py:717`)
  validates only the PRIVATE key (present / 0600 / Ed25519 / not-encrypted, via `compose_signer`)
  and aborts startup on an unusable signer — it never checks that a public counterpart is
  resolvable.

These are `static` (content) hypotheses, confirmed by source + reference-set inspection; there is
no runtime failure to reproduce because the whole defect is a SILENCE.

### Legitimacy: `incomplete-implementation` (cited), NOT a fresh feature request

Design authority establishing these guards were *meant to exist*:
- Parent bug `d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a` (`dire-expectable-terrapin`), closed `plan_defect`, explicitly
  scoped **AC5 (mint-time WARNING) + AC6 (deploy/startup health check)** and SPLIT them into this
  ticket as "additive guards against the class regressing." That parent plan passed plan-review.
- Designed-but-unwired seams already in-repo: the verify-side `_opcert_own_public_keys` resolver
  (AC1), the `run_startup_store_sweep` startup-warning idiom (AC1), and the fail-closed startup
  validator `compose_startup_opcert_binding` (AC3).

So approval is NOT the open question → not a `feature-request`, not `intended-behavior`. This is a
deferred, scoped omission = `incomplete-implementation`.

**Attribution (scope-of-work).** This is an omission, so there is no introducing commit that
"broke" it. By scope-of-work it attributes to `d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a` — the ticket whose acceptance
criteria (AC5/AC6) the missing behaviour falls under, which shipped the key-resolution fix without
these deferred guards.

### Why I am ESCALATING rather than auto-fixing (per operator instruction)

The mint-time warning (AC1/AC2) is cleanly auto-fixable: purely additive, non-refusing, fully
pinned by the cited authority (warn, naming the resolved key path + principal; do not refuse; the
existing success path and returned signature are unchanged). Mirrors `run_startup_store_sweep`.

**AC3 is NOT pinned by the cited authority** — it "requires a design decision" and "alters
deploy-time behaviour," which the operator reserved for themselves. AC3 says the health check
"FAILS," but the repo contains TWO deliberate, conflicting precedents:

- **(a) Hard-abort startup** — extend the existing fail-closed `compose_startup_opcert_binding`
  (which already aborts on an unusable signer). Scoped to the on-box signing deploy only (both
  `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` set); dev/stdio/genesis returns `None`
  early and is unaffected; a correctly-configured deploy (post-2337, which derives the public line
  in-process) still passes. Only a misconfigured signing deploy newly refuses to serve.
- **(b) Report a degraded field, never abort** — mirror `store_status` / `/health` +
  blue-green readiness gate. `_mcp_health.py` documents the explicit invariant: "a health probe
  that can fail is worse than one that reports a degraded field," and `run_startup_store_sweep` is
  log-and-continue ("a missing store must not abort boot"; only `RemovedInputError` fails hard).

These behave materially differently on a misconfigured deploy (refuse-to-serve vs serve-degraded),
and the choice is not resolved by the cited authority. Per the operating instruction to escalate
design decisions / behaviour changes, I am handing this call to the operator.

**Recommendation:** proceed on AC1/AC2 as specified; for AC3 adopt **option (a)** (extend
`compose_startup_opcert_binding`, gated on the on-box signing deploy) — it is the closest existing
precedent ("an unusable signer aborts startup"), fail-closed matches the parent bug's whole point
(silently-uncertifiable attestations are worse than a refused boot), and it has zero blast radius
on dev/stdio and on correctly-configured deploys. If the operator prefers non-aborting deploy
posture, option (b) is the alternative. Awaiting direction before Phase 2 / any Gerrit push.
No `--force` or gate bypass was used; no code change pushed.

comments.body:
Phase 2 complete — fix pushed to Gerrit change 2360.

## Root cause (proven, Phase 1)
The op-cert signing subsystem had NO guard surfacing a signing key whose public
counterpart the same-environment verify path cannot resolve. `mint_opcert_record`
(_opcert_signing.py) never consulted `_opcert_own_public_keys` (its sole caller was
the verify path, :550), and no counterpart check existed in mcp_server.py /
_mcp_health.py / _opcert_binding.py. This is the exact divergence class Gerrit 2337
(parent d26a) fixed — write-side key resolution diverging from verify-side resolution
so signing succeeds but verify returns `foreign_key` and the claim gate refuses every
ticket — with nothing to surface it. Genuine omission.

## Classification & legitimacy
`incomplete-implementation` (NOT feature-request): parent d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a
(dire-expectable-terrapin, closed plan_defect) explicitly SPLIT its deferred AC5
(mint-time warning) + AC6 (startup health check) into THIS ticket as "additive guards
against the class regressing." Design authority cited → completing/wiring the approved
work is restoration, not creation.

## Fix (per the operator's reframed AC3)
Two additive, NON-REFUSING guards:
- AC1/AC2 (mint warning): `_warn_if_verify_cannot_resolve` in `mint_opcert_record`
  logs a WARNING naming key_path + principal when the same-env verify resolver cannot
  resolve a public counterpart for the key just signed under; still returns the
  signature. Silent on the healthy path.
- AC3 (serve-degraded, NEVER abort): `opcert_signing_status` /
  `opcert_signer_degraded` / `run_startup_opcert_check` in `_mcp_health.py` check the
  ONE non-redundant condition the derived-key path can't catch: does the bound signer's
  public key match the pinned `rebar.attest.trusted_env` key for its principal. Exposed
  as a `/health` "opcert" field + a boot warning. `expected` gates strictness like
  `store_status` (only when `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` is present), because
  required-env binding is advisory today (ADR 0104 dec. 3). Did NOT extend
  `compose_startup_opcert_binding` to abort; did NOT add a redundant derive probe.

## Test (RED->GREEN, held-out, mutation-checked)
`tests/unit/test_opcert_public_counterpart_guard_879b.py` (7 tests). Seen RED first
(AC1 on assertion `[]`; AC3 on AttributeError = capability absent), GREEN after.
Mutation check (sandboxed, sandbox-exec): removing the mint guard -> AC1 RED; forcing
`opcert_signer_degraded` False -> both AC3 degraded tests RED; restored -> GREEN. Tests
assert observable output (log messages / dict fields), not private names.

## Scope & safety
- Caller sweep: production explicit-signer paths run inside `bound_signer(signer)`
  (jobs.py:91), so the mint guard's resolver won't false-warn. All production
  environment self-signing funnels through the guarded `mint_opcert_record`.
- Restoration not creation (cited design authority d26a); no new dependency (all
  imports pre-existing); no pre-existing test weakened.
- Regression sweep: 349 passed / 3 skipped across opcert/mcp_health/trusted_env/signing.
  Lint + typecheck clean. Non-test diff 109 lines (< 150 floor -> no review-plan needed).

## Siblings (Step 7)
- Axis 1 (construct): the only environment-derivation mint path is `mint_opcert_record`
  -- covered. No other instances.
- Axis 2 (parity): `sign_opcert_manifest` (:611) signs an op-cert bypassing the guard,
  but it takes an EXPLICIT caller-supplied key and has NO production caller (test/remote-
  cert primitive, keystone e4df) used to sign under deliberately foreign/remote keys.
  879b's env-derivation divergence cannot arise there, and the same-env warning would
  false-positive on foreign-key signing -> N/A by design, not MISSING. `/health` is the
  single health surface; status stashed for both http + stdio.

## Defect origin
Attributed by scope-of-work to d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a (the parent that scoped AC5/AC6 and
deferred them into this ticket). Omission -> no introducing commit; will be recorded via
the non-gated `--caused-by=d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a` on close. `caused_by` link already
recorded in Phase 1.

## Replication
Original report ("no guard surfaces a signing key with no usable public cert") no longer
holds: the mint path warns, and `/health` reports a degraded `opcert` field + boot
warning on the pinned-key mismatch.

## Gerrit
Change 2360 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2360 — awaiting
LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 before Submit.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Split out of `d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a` (`dire-expectable-terrapin`), where these were carried as
its DEFERRED AC5 and AC6. That bug fixed the key-path DIVERGENCE that made the deployed MCP
server sign op-certs it could never verify (Gerrit 2337, merged as
`83edf9972728ae1e0729a39098ec70e4fab4617a`): verification now resolves the public half from the
same ordered chain the signing side resolves the private half.

What that fix did NOT add is any GUARD. `sign_manifest` still mints a certificate without
checking that the environment can resolve a public counterpart for the key it just signed
under, and nothing at deploy/startup surfaces it when it cannot. So the CLASS of defect — a
silently uncertifiable attestation — can regress the moment a new deployment shape puts the
signing key somewhere the resolution chain does not reach. Signing succeeds; only a later
`verify_signature` (or a refused claim) reveals the problem, potentially long after the
certificates were minted.

## Approach
Two independent, additive guards, neither of which changes an existing success path:

1. At MINT: after `ensure_opcert_key` resolves the SPECIFIC signing key path used for this
   mint, read THAT key's own public line with `_read_opcert_pub(key_path)` and check whether it
   is a MEMBER of the verify-side resolvable set `_opcert_own_public_keys`
   (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`). Matching is on the key TYPE+BASE64 BODY (comment-
   insensitive), mirroring ssh `allowed_signers`. The check is membership of the specific
   signing key's public counterpart, NOT merely the non-emptiness of the aggregate chain — a
   chain where a DIFFERENT key resolves a pub must NOT satisfy the guard for the key actually
   signed under. When the specific key's counterpart is absent, emit an explicit WARNING naming
   the resolved key path and the principal. It must NOT refuse — refusing would break every
   existing sign flow and is a behaviour change beyond this bug's scope.

   Worked example (specification by example). Own-key chain = [binding-key `K_b`, genesis
   `K_g`]. `ensure_opcert_key` selects `K_g` for this mint (binding absent), but only `K_b`'s
   `.pub` is derivable (K_g lives on a path the resolver cannot reach). Aggregate
   `_opcert_own_public_keys` = {body(K_b)} — NON-EMPTY. A non-emptiness check would stay
   SILENT (wrong). The specified membership check computes `body(_read_opcert_pub(path_of
   K_g))` ∉ {body(K_b)} → WARNS (correct), naming `path_of K_g` and the principal.

2. At STARTUP/DEPLOY: the MCP server's existing health surface (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`)
   reports a DEGRADED field and logs a boot WARNING when the bound startup signer's public key
   is not the pinned trusted-environment key for its principal — the ONE same-environment
   failure the (derivative) public key cannot otherwise catch. SERVE-DEGRADED, never abort
   boot (operator ruling; ADR 0104 decision 3 makes required-environment binding advisory
   today), mirroring `store_status` / `run_startup_store_sweep`.

Both are in-process checks driven by an operation and by server startup, with no dependency on
any particular CI provider.

### AC3 reframing (operator ruling, recorded here)
The op-cert public key is DERIVATIVE (`_derive_opcert_pub` = `ssh-keygen -y`, re-derivable on
demand from the private key), and `compose_startup_opcert_binding` already fails closed on a
bad/missing/encrypted/non-Ed25519 private key. So a "can we resolve/derive a public cert?"
startup probe would be REDUNDANT. The one genuinely non-redundant condition is whether the
bound signer's public key MATCHES the environment's pinned/published trusted-environment key
(`rebar.attest.trusted_env`) — the key required-environment verify checks against. Even that is
non-blocking: those are still valid signed attestations that only fail an advisory
environment-binding check, so AC3 emits a degraded health field + a warning and does NOT refuse
to serve or abort boot.

## Scope
- In scope: the mint-time warning and the startup/health serve-degraded surface.
- Out of scope: the key-resolution chain itself (already fixed by 2337); any change to the
  cross-environment `foreign_key` verdict, which is documented intended behaviour (ADR 0104),
  not a defect; extending `compose_startup_opcert_binding` to abort; a redundant derive probe.

## Testing
Unit tests: a mint under a key whose SPECIFIC public half cannot be resolved (even when another
chain key's pub resolves) emits the warning and still returns a signature; a mint under a
resolvable key emits no warning; the startup/health check reports degraded (and warns) for a
bound signer whose public key is not the pinned key, and is quiet/non-degraded for a matched
key, for an unbound signer, and for a deployment that has not opted into pinning; key matching
is on the key type+base64 body (comment-insensitive); a resolution fault is surfaced as
degraded (not swallowed); a `RemovedInputError` fails hard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1: `sign_manifest` emits an explicit WARNING — naming the resolved signing key path and the principal — when the SPECIFIC key it just signed under has no public counterpart in the verify-side resolvable set (`_read_opcert_pub(key_path)` body ∉ `_opcert_own_public_keys`), even if a different chain key's pub resolves; it still returns the signature (no refusal, no existing sign flow broken).
- [x] AC2: `sign_manifest` emits no such warning when the specific signing key's public counterpart IS resolvable.
- [x] AC3: the MCP server's startup/health surface reports a DEGRADED `opcert` field and logs a boot WARNING when the bound signer's public key is not the pinned trusted-environment key for its principal, and is non-degraded/quiet when it matches (or when unbound / pinning not configured). Non-blocking: it NEVER aborts boot (serve-degraded; ADR 0104 decision 3).
- [x] AC4: both guards are in-process and operation-linked, with no dependency on a specific CI provider.

## Definition of Done
- [x] DD1: AC1 and AC2 covered by a test that is RED before the change and GREEN after it, including the specific-key case where a different chain key's pub resolves (aggregate non-empty) yet the signed key's own counterpart is absent.
- [x] DD2: AC3 covered by a test over the startup/health check (degraded, matched, unbound, and not-pinned cases).
- [x] DD3: AC4 verified by the observable proxy that both guards execute with no CI-provider environment present — the unit tests exercise mint and startup/health with no CI env vars set and assert the warning/degraded behaviour purely from in-process log/dict output (no network, no CI API), confirming operation/startup-linked triggers.

file_impact.reason: AC1/AC2: mint-time WARNING guard (_warn_if_verify_cannot_resolve) + _ssh_pub_body key-body normalization helper. Same-environment verify subsystem extracted to _opcert_verify.py for the 800-LOC module-size cap after rebasing onto a grown origin/main.

Module-size split of _opcert_signing.py: same-environment verify path (verify_opcert_record + _opcert_subject_binding_error/_required_environment/_pinned_environment_keys/_opcert_trust_root) moved verbatim along the existing mint/verify call-graph seam; re-exported from _opcert_signing. No behaviour change.

AC3: serve-degraded startup/health surface wired into /health + run_mcp; opcert-health symbols extracted to _mcp_opcert_health.py for the 800-LOC module-size cap after rebasing onto a grown origin/main (handshake subsystem).
Module-size split of _mcp_health.py: the 4 opcert-health symbols (opcert_signing_status/opcert_signer_degraded/run_startup_opcert_check/_OPCERT_STATUS_ATTR) moved verbatim. No behaviour change.
RED->GREEN oracle for AC1-AC3 incl. comment-insensitive match, error-degraded, and RemovedInputError re-raise regressions.
